title: BW-ORG-v1 (v2.6)
description: Organisation Profile: display metadata, roles, acceptance policies (evaluated over MLS group acknowledgements), an optional designated EP authority, and (v2.0) an optional confidentiality-scope map (spec §8.3a). v1.2 makes the acceptance policy deterministic: sealed as a COSE_Sign1 artefact, versioned (policy_version, valid_from), and referenced from SE/DE via acceptance_policy_ref (spec §8.3). v1.4 adds the optional delivery_grades map (spec §8.3b): the per-content-class delivery grade; availability is never a default. v1.5 adds the optional per-scope human_acceptance flag (Annex R, A3): system members are excluded from a human-gated scope's acceptance eligible set. v1.6 adds the per-scope records_role field (F16): which org role is a records scope's records leaf.

policy_version.description: Monotonic version identifier of this organisation profile / acceptance policy (spec §8.3). Referenced by SE/DE acceptance_policy_ref.

valid_from.description: Instant from which this policy_version is in force. R4-U1: the window is [valid_from, successor.valid_from) and the upper bound is DERIVED FROM THE CHAIN, never stored here. A published BW-ORG is IMMUTABLE — writing an end date into it later changes its deterministic-CBOR digest, and evidence that pinned the document would stop resolving to it. R4-02 reproduced exactly that deadlock: leaving v1 unbounded made the chain reject it ("has a successor but no valid_until"), and bounding it changed its digest, so both branches were closed for the ordinary publication.

additionalProperties.description: any-one | all | quorum:n | device-class:<class>. Evaluated over MLS group acknowledgements by RDP(in) alone — the sole evidence-authoritative evaluator (X-10; TS clause 6). The MSP collects and forwards member confirmations; it evaluates nothing. X-16: the KEY is a RoleName — every declared role is addressable as bw:...r/<role>.

acceptance_policy.description: X-12 (BW-ORG 2.4): the RoleName-keyed acceptance-policy map, REQUIRED and non-empty, with the reserved key `default` REQUIRED — the policy governing entity-addressed default-scope messages, its eligible set the ENTIRE active membership. Exactly one key governs every message via the umbrella §8.3 deterministic selection: scoped → the scope's acceptance_policy_ref key; default-scope role-addressed → the role's key if present, else `default`; default-scope entity-addressed → `default`.

scope_map.description: Optional confidentiality-scope map (spec §8.3a). Signed as part of this BW-ORG document; the scope version in force at submission is echoed in SE/DE scope_ref. Absent ⇒ default-scope-only (backwards compatible). Administered by the same authority that seals this document (D3).

fallback.description: Map-level fallback (D4): when present, a content class with no matching scope MAY fall back to the default scope. Absent ⇒ no map-level fallback (submission refused with no-matching-scope unless a per-scope fallback applies).

member_endpoint.description: Base URL of the entity's member-enumeration surface (edd-resolver GET /uid/{uid}/members; umbrella §8.3a, F14): the active members with roles and per-device MLS leaf-node references and capabilities, so a counterparty can resolve the scope-eligible member/device set and a verifier can map group leaves to members and roles. REQUIRED where a scope_map is published (discovery_lint LINT-DISC-19). A non-authoritative discovery mirror — each member's sealed BW-MEMBER-v1 remains the trust anchor.

delivery_grades.description: OPTIONAL per-content-class delivery-grade declaration (spec §8.3b, v1.4): which act makes delivery of the class legally operative. Only classes explicitly listed here with the value 'availability' are availability-grade — never a default; undeclared classes take the grade implied by the governing acceptance policy (any-one/device-class => verification; quorum/all => acceptance). Grade/policy coherence: LINT-DISC-18.

max_ttl.description: OPTIONAL (X-22, v2.2): the maximum TTL this entity accepts for inbound messages, as an ISO 8601 duration (days/time designators, e.g. P30D, P7D, PT72H). Absent = the profile default P30D. At submission the sender-computed expires_at MUST satisfy sent_at < expires_at <= sent_at + max_ttl (bundle_lint LINT-BND-27; the SE-level ordering is evidence_lint LINT-DE-18).

supersedes.description: R4-U1: the predecessor this version replaces, pinned by CONTENT. This is now the ONLY statement of where the predecessor's window ends: `v2.valid_from` IS the instant v1 ceased. The digest is what makes the chain non-equivocable — an entity cannot publish two documents claiming the same predecessor without the disagreement being visible WHEN BOTH ARE OBSERVED. It does not PREVENT equivocation; that needs transparency and remains X-33.

doc_digest.description: SHA-256 of the predecessor's deterministic-CBOR body — the same digest acceptance_policy_ref pins.

ScopeDescriptor.description: A named confidentiality boundary (spec §8.3a). One MLS group per (entity pair, scope). recoverability is explicit with no default (D2).

scope_id.description: Stable scope identifier (e.g. 'legal', 'finance'). 'default' is RESERVED for the implicit baseline scope and MUST NOT be declared here (spec §8.3a).

version.description: Monotonic descriptor version; the value in force at submission is echoed in SE/DE scope_ref.

roles.description: Roles whose members' devices are eligible leaves of this scope's group. X-16: each is a RoleName (addressable).

content_classes.description: Envelope content_class values that route to this scope. Two-tier registry (the I-D, IANA Considerations): standard federation-governed classes, or entity-defined private classes under the mandatory x- prefix; the registry-membership discipline is discovery_lint LINT-DISC-16.

recoverability.description: REQUIRED, no default (D2): strict = only role members' devices; records = a declared organisational records/compliance leaf is present in the group and MUST be visible in the roster.

acceptance_policy_ref.description: Reference to the acceptance rule applied WITHIN this scope (quorum counts scope members only).

fallback.description: Per-scope fallback declaration (D4). Absent ⇒ no fallback for this scope.

human_acceptance.description: OPTIONAL (default false; Annex R, A3): when true, legal acceptance in this scope requires a human — system members (member_type=system) are EXCLUDED from the scope's acceptance eligible set (§8.3), so an agent's acknowledgement does not satisfy the class. A human-acceptance scope whose eligible set is entirely system members is unsatisfiable (bundle_lint LINT-BND-16).

records_role.description: The organisation role whose active members are this scope's RECORDS LEAF (F16, §8.3a). X-16: a RoleName (addressable). REQUIRED where recoverability=records, FORBIDDEN where recoverability=strict (discovery_lint LINT-DISC-21). MUST be a declared org role and MUST NOT be one of this scope's own roles[] — the records function RECOVERS but is NOT an acceptance party (SCOPE-8 counts scope-role holders only). Distinguishability is the role, resolved via the member-enumeration surface (leaf → member → roles, §8.3a F14): a records scope's roster is exactly {scope-role holders} ∪ {records_role holders}.
